note: Every date drawn has two sources, named in sources{} by key. 'lo'/'hi' bound an uncertain date; a soft end is drawn across that range. A date given as one year in both sources is drawn sharp.

sources.SEP-M: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Marcus Aurelius' (plato.stanford.edu/entries/marcus-aurelius/), read 2026-11-17
sources.IEP-M: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Marcus Aurelius' (iep.utm.edu/marcus/), read 2026-11-17
sources.LIV: Livius.org, 'Marcus Aurelius' (Jona Lendering; chronology section), read 2026-11-17
sources.FRONTO: Fronto, Ad M. Caesarem 4.13, Marcus to Fronto: 'at twenty-five years of age' (romanletters.org/letters/fronto/fronto.ad.m.caes.iv.13/, dated there c. 147, and 145-147 in the 19th-century translation), read 2026-11-17
sources.WIKI-M: Wikipedia, 'Marcus Aurelius': 'By the age of twenty-five (between April 146 and April 147)', footnoted to Birley, Marcus Aurelius, p. 69; plague 'broke out in 165 or 166'; read 2026-11-17
sources.MED-1.7: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations 1.7, George Long's translation (classics.mit.edu): Rusticus, 'I am indebted to him for being acquainted with the discourses of Epictetus, which he communicated to me out of his own collection'; read 2026-11-17
sources.WIKI-R: Wikipedia, 'Quintus Junius Rusticus', quoting Meditations 1.7 and Historia Augusta, Marcus 3; gives no year for the lending; read 2026-11-17
sources.MED-HEADS: Meditations, end of Book 1 'Among the Quadi at the Granua' and end of Book 2 'This in Carnuntum' (Long, classics.mit.edu), read 2026-11-17
sources.DJ: Richard Duncan-Jones, 'The Antonine Plague Revisited', Arctos 52 (2018), § 2 Chronicle of Events: '165 Plague in the east at Nisibis and Smyrna', '165/6 brought back to Rome', '182 ... Bedaium', '189 At Rome, the worst plague outbreak known to Dio'; read 2026-11-17
sources.WIKI-MW: Wikipedia, 'Marcomannic Wars': 'AD 166-180', 'a series of wars lasting from about CE 166 until 180'; read 2026-11-17
sources.DIO-72: Cassius Dio, Roman History, epitome of Book 72 (Loeb, LacusCurtius) § 33: 'he passed away on the seventeenth of March'; § 34: 'emperor himself nineteen years and eleven days'; read 2026-11-17
sources.EUS-5.1: Eusebius, Church History 5.1.1 (trans. McGiffert, NPNF, newadvent.org): 'In the seventeenth year of the Emperor Antoninus Verus ... Gaul, of which Lyons and Vienne are the principal'; the seventeenth year of a reign begun 161 is 177; read 2026-11-17
sources.WIKI-E: Wikipedia, 'Epictetus': 'Around AD 93, when the Roman emperor Domitian banished all philosophers from the city'; 'He died sometime around AD 135'; read 2026-11-17

born.label: born c. 50s, Hierapolis; a slave, later freed (SEP: 'spent a portion of his life as the slave of Epaphroditus', 'the freedman philosopher')

banished.label: banished from Italy; teaches at Nicopolis, Greece
src: IEP-E 'in about 89 ... banished by the Emperor Domitian'
banished.doubt: SEP and IEP give 89; Wikipedia gives 'around AD 93'. Drawn c. 89 with a soft end running to 95.

arrian.label: Arrian writes down his lectures
src: SEP-E 'around the year 108 by Millar's (1965) dating'
IEP-E 'some time around the years 104-107' (a conjecture)

adopted.label: adopted into the succession
src: IEP-M 'adopted by the Emperor Antoninus Pius in 138 C.E.'

rusticus.label: Rusticus lends him notes of Epictetus's lectures

died.label: dies on the frontier
src: DIO-72 'the seventeenth of March'; 'nineteen years and eleven days' from 7 March 161
died.doubt: Place: Vindobona (Livius) or Sirmium (Wikipedia lists both); Dio does not say. Drawn as 'on the frontier'.

plague.label: the Antonine plague, from 165/6
src: DJ '165 Plague in the east'; '165/6 brought back to Rome'; outbreaks in 182 and 189
plague.doubt: It runs past the frame: Duncan-Jones lists outbreaks in 182 and 189. Drawn as continuing past 180.

wars.label: war on the northern frontier
src: LIV '169 ... leaves Rome for war against the Germanic tribes'; '179 continued war'; '180 ... dies in Vindobona'
wars.doubt: The wars began c. 166 with crossings of the frontier; Marcus himself left Rome for them in 169 (Livius). Soft start 166-169.

meds.label: the Meditations written, in the field
src: IEP-M 'probably written while Marcus was on campaign in central Europe, c. C.E. 171-175'
SEP-M 'written during the last years of his military campaigns'
MED-HEADS 'Among the Quadi at the Granua'; 'This in Carnuntum'
meds.doubt: Scholars' dates vary: IEP c. 171-175, Livius begun 174, SEP 'the last years of his military campaigns' (to 180). Drawn as a soft span 170-180 with no sharp ends.
